subject: Post-demo: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — next tests & incident response details
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
Date: 2025-06-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — next tests & incident response details

Hi Alex — thanks for the time today, appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap:
- You were primarily focused on predictable latency at scale, cost/unit token economics, and incident handling (RCA and escalation paths).
- You called out two main alternatives you're evaluating: AWS SageMaker endpoints / Bedrock and OpenAI's API.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical experiement: we can run a 48h latency + throughput test against a set of representative requests you provide (we'll run identical prompt traffic against Redwood and one hyperscaler). We'll capture P50/P95/P99, cold-start behavior, and cost estimates. (SE support included.)
2) Incident SLAs & RCA: I'll share our incident response matrix and SOC2 summary; Dev will detail on-call and escalation flow.
3) Contract/terms: Jonas (cc) can provide standard Dedicated terms if you want to explore reserved capacity.

Attachments: will follow in a separate email — one-pager & SOC2 summary.

Do these next steps look right? If yes, can you confirm the test window you prefer (this week/day next) and share a small sample of prompts + expected QPS?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.ai>

Date: 2025-06-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — next tests & incident response details

Marissa — thanks, that looks good. A few clarifying questions before we lock the test window: 

1) Test scope: can you run both text-generation and embeddings workloads in the same 48h window, or do you recommend separate runs? Our plan is primarily generation at ~30 RPS peak and embeddings at ~10 RPS steady.
2) Cost comparatives: for hyperscalers we can get published token/unit prices but we care about real-perf cost (i.e., effective $/successful-response measured). Will you produce a cost-per-1M-token-style estimate based on the test?
3) Incident response: we require an SLA for production incidents (P1/P2 definitions) — what are typical Redwood response and mitigation timelines, and can you provide an example RCA template? Our procurement/security team has asked specifically how you compare to AWS SLAs + support levels.

If you can answer the above we can pick a slot. Prefer 6/16-6/17 for the test window (PDT).

— Alex
Alex Chen
Head of ML Engineering | Acme AI
alex.chen@acme.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
Date: 2025-06-13T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — next tests & incident response details

Alex — great questions, answered inline below and proposed concrete plan. See attached one-pager for a concise comparison vs hyperscalers.

> 1) Can you run both generation and embeddings in the same 48h window?
Yes — we can run both workloads in the same window. We'll partition the window (first 24h gen, second 24h embeddings) or run mixed traffic if you prefer. For comparability, mixed traffic with your representative distribution is fine. Please send 1-2 sample prompt sets and the target QPS profile.

> 2) Cost comparatives: will you produce cost-per-1M-token estimate?
Yes — our test report includes:
- Observed P50/P95/P99 latency at target QPS
- Effective $/response and $/1M effective tokens (we include infra + queuing amortized costs)
- Cold-start and KV cache hit impact on cost

> 3) Incident response & RCA: what are timelines and can you provide template?
High level:
- Support tiers: Hosted API (business hours SLA), Dedicated (24/7 support + faster response SLAs), Private (enterprise SLA options).
- Typical response times (Dedicated): P1 initial ack < 15 min, mitigation action within 1 hour, ongoing updates every 30 min until mitigated. RCA delivered within 72 hours of mitigation with follow-up postmortem within 7 business days.
- We'll provide our RCA template and an example (redacted). For hyperscalers: their default managed endpoints often rely on multi-day RCAs and support plan level impacts timeline — we'll call this out in the one-pager.

Concrete next steps:
- Dev will propose a short test plan and the exact metric collection endpoints. (see Dev's email below with attachments)
- If 6/16-6/17 works we can reserve capacity and share test endpoints by end of day 6/15.

Attached: Redwood_vs_Hyperscalers_OnePager.pdf (one-page comparison).

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — next tests & incident response details

Alex / team — Dev here, solutions engineer. Attaching a short test plan and our SOC2 summary. High-level technical notes below and the incident response table you asked for.

Test plan (attached: Redwood_Test_Plan_Seed.xlsx):
- Ingress: we'll provide HTTPS endpoints and a small client harness (k6 or locust scripts) to drive your prompts at desired QPS.
- Metrics: token counts, per-request latency (P50/P95/P99), GPU util, queue length, cold-start latency, error rates.
- Cost calc: we snapshot instance usage+GPU hour cost and map to effective $/1M tokens.
- Comparison: we'll run the same harness against your AWS/Bedrock setup (if you provide access or run the harness) or alternatively run both sides with identical synthetic load.

Incident response & escalation (summary):
- Definitions:
  - P1: Production outage impacting >50% of requests or total service unavailability.
  - P2: Severe degradation impacting a subset of traffic (error spike, high latency).
- Redwood Dedicated SLA (summary):
  - Initial ack: < 15 minutes (pager on-call)
  - Triage & mitigation action: < 1 hour
  - Status updates: every 30 minutes until steady-state
  - RCA: initial RCA within 72 hours, full postmortem within 7 business days
- Hyperscaler (typical observed):
  - Initial ack: 15-60 minutes depending on support tier
  - RCA: often initial RCA takes multiple days; full postmortem on different cadence and may be less specific about host-level details due to shared infra

Notes on RCA content we provide (attached: Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf includes examples):
- Timeline of events with timestamps
- Root cause analysis and contributing factors
- Mitigation steps taken and permanent fixes planned
- Customer-facing impact summary and remediation timeline

If you want, we can run the test in a canary fashion: route 10% of your traffic through Redwood for 24h and then increase. That gives a realistic risk-limited view.

I'll coordinate generating test endpoints if 6/16-6/17 is confirmed — let me know preferred start time (PDT).

— Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.inference

- For the canary option: if we start with 10% traffic through Redwood, can you confirm how routing latency is measured end-to-end so we can align instrumentation?

I'll get the prompt sets and QPS profile to you by EOD today. Looking forward.

— Alex
